author: Agencies
description:
Quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region with a depth of 10km early on Saturday morning

A powerful 7.7-magnitude quake has struck off the coast of Indonesia, the US Geological Survey said. No immediate casualties or damage were reported.

The quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region with a depth of 10km at 5:58am on Saturday Indonesia time. It’s epicentre was 68km (42 miles) north-northwest of the city of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara province.

Continue reading...
title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off coast of Indonesia and tsunami warning issued

author: Marina Dunbar and Joseph Gedeon
description:
President said nine months at sea ‘not nearly long enough’ even as families call for attention to mental health crisis

Donald Trump has downplayed concerns about US sailors enduring a record-setting deployment of nearly nine months aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln on Friday, saying the deployment is “not nearly long enough” as concerns mount over mental health and supply issues aboard the aircraft carrier.

The US president made the comments during a brief exchange with reporters before flying to New York for an event highlighting falling violent crime rates across the US.

Continue reading...
title: Trump downplays concerns about sailors aboard USS Abraham Lincoln amid record deployment

author: Aletha Adu
description:
PM steps up climate response with measures including better water access and support for building farm reservoirs

Farmers must not carry the risks of the climate crisis alone, Andy Burnham has said, as he announced £65m of funding to help them manage the devastating drought.

The prime minister is stepping up his response to the immediate climate crisis after facing a backlash from his own MPs and Labour’s grassroots for not addressing the climate crisis despite wildfires tearing through Britain and a drought affecting food producers. Labour MPs argued Burnham had taken too long to talk about the climate crisis and had not made it a priority.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham announces £65m for drought-hit farmers after Labour pressure

author: Maya Yang
description:
Seriousness of remark made in New York on Friday, and whether it signaled new policy ​position, not clear

Donald Trump has threatened to declare the strait of Hormuz as “a territory of the United States” as his administration struggles to conclude the war with Iran.

During a speech at a police academy on Long Island, New York, on Friday, the US president said he would “pretty soon” designate the waterway – a crucial chokepoint for global trade, through which about a fifth of the world’s seaborne oil supplies typically pass – a US territory.

Continue reading...
title: Trump threatens to declare strait of Hormuz ‘territory of the United States’

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
Network wants to serve Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr after president sues over January 6 documentary

The BBC is trying to subpoena Donald Trump’s children as it builds its defense against the president’s defamation lawsuit centered on a documentary on the January 6 insurrection.

In a motion filed Friday, the BBC sought authorization to serve Trump’s two eldest children, Donald Trump Jr and Ivanka Trump, and son-in-law Jared Kushner, with subpoenas for testimony and their records on the events of 6 January 2021.

Continue reading...
title: BBC seeks to subpoena Trump’s eldest children and son-in-law over defamation lawsuit

author: Olivia Bowden
description:
Win is significant for region’s premier, Doug Ford, who blames protected zones for city’s traffic ills

The Ontario government is now free to rip out Toronto’s bike lanes on its busiest streets after the region’s top court ruled in favour of the province on Friday, overturning a lower court’s decision that decreed removal would violate constitutional rights.

The win is significant for Ontario’s premier, Doug Ford, and his government, who have long railed against Toronto’s bike lanes, blaming the protected zones for the city’s traffic ills.

Continue reading...
title: Ontario free to axe Toronto bike lanes, region’s top court rules

author: Richard Adams
description:
Academic was pronounced dead at his home in south London after police called to address after 3pm on Friday

Jason Arday, the black academic who resigned last week as a professor at the University of Cambridge, has been found dead at his home in south London.

The Metropolitan police said officers were called to Arday’s address by the London ambulance service after 3pm on Friday.

Continue reading...
title: Jason Arday found dead after resigning from Cambridge over plagiarism claims

author: Aletha Adu
description:
People urged not to light barbecues, campfires or anything else that could spark fire during period of extreme heat

Millions of people across England and Wales have received an emergency alert to their phones as the government warns against activities that could start fires.

The deputy prime minister, Louise Haigh, said it was the most extensive use to date of the emergency alert system, with phones beaming a siren noise about 7pm, with the warning “there is a serious risk of wildfires nationally”.

Continue reading...
title: Emergency alert warning of wildfire risk sent to phones in England and Wales

author: Anna Betts
description:
Michael Boren requested more aircraft for 7-acre Cabin Creek fire, some of which were diverted from other fires

Michael Boren, the US undersecretary of agriculture for natural resources and environment who oversees the US Forest Service, reportedly pressed agency staff last month to deploy more aircraft to a 7-acre (2.8-hectare) fire that was burning near his Idaho ranch, according to a Washington Post report on Friday.

The Cabin Creek fire in Idaho began on about 12 July as a result of an unattended campfire, and spread across several acres in Idaho’s
title: US forest service chief reportedly pressed staff for more support for wildfire near his ranch

author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
description:
Thursday has been described by residents as ‘horrendous’, ‘distressing’ and ‘one of the scariest days of my life’

People in Stourbridge have described the fires that devastated more than a dozen homes as “horrendous” and “distressing”, with one describing blazes that surpassed the height of residential houses.

Multiple fires spread across the West Midlands on Thursday as temperatures reached record highs of 38.1C in the UK, during the country’s fifth consecutive heatwave.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s due to climate’: the people of Stourbridge on the town’s wildfires

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Facility also had no air conditioning for two days amid extreme heat, according to one of the people detained

People detained at an overcrowded federal immigration camp in Mississippi were sickened by a mystery gas leak, then denied medical care when they complained of headaches and other symptoms, it has been alleged.

A lengthy power outage at Adams county detention center, an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility run by the private operator CoreCivic, also left it without air conditioning for two days this week, according to one detainee who contacted the Guardian through his family.

Continue reading...
title: People detained at Mississippi ICE facility sickened by gas leak and denied medical care

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
Group backs Elijah Manley in primary election in bid to unseat veteran Democrat in newly drawn district

A progressive group has endorsed a 27-year-old substitute teacher who overcame childhood homelessness in his bid to unseat the veteran Democrat Debbie Wasserman Schultz in Florida.

The Progressive Change Campaign Committee (PCCC) said it was backing Elijah Manley in next week’s primary election in Florida’s newly drawn 20th congressional district, casting the race as a contest between a young economic populist and a stalwart of the Democratic party establishment.

Continue reading...
title: Progressives back substitute teacher over Wasserman Schultz in Florida

author: Olivia Bowden in Toronto
description:
Government launches investigation into potential unsafe practices at Spanish healthcare company Grifols

A chain of private plasma donation clinics in Canada said Friday it is pausing collections after the deaths of two donors and a new government investigation into potential unsafe practices.

Grifols, the Spanish healthcare company that runs 17 clinics across Canada and is the country’s only private clinic for plasma donation, said it informed Health Canada of its decision to temporarily pause collections on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
title: Canadian plasma clinics pause collections after deaths of two donors

author: Aisha Down
description:
Planning consultation told ‘robust security measures’ will be needed amid growing resistance to such developments

Scottish police have warned that a proposed datacentre will require “robust security measures” to prevent “incursion” amid growing public resistance to such developments in Scotland.

“A great deal of public opposition is likely” to a datacentre planned in Larbert, about 30 miles west of Edinburgh, the Scottish police have said in a letter submitted as a part of a planning consultation earlier this month.

Continue reading...
title: Scottish police expect ‘great deal of public opposition’ to planned Larbert datacentre

author: Richard Adams Education editor
description:
Students narrowly missing grades are being rejected, while some on oversubscribed courses are asked to defer

Students across the UK have found themselves unexpectedly squeezed out of their desired university courses as this year’s bumper crop of A-level grades ​h​as not always translated into ​​the places many were hoping for.

​With close to a third of the A-levels awarded in England, Wales and Northern Ireland achieving the top A and A* grades this year, universities are taking a tougher stance by rejecting students who narrowly missed their expected grades and who in previous years would still have gained a place.

Continue reading...
title: Students squeezed out of university courses after bumper A-level grades

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Biological parents given custody of child born in Texas amid dispute over surrogate mother’s claim of abortion request

A two-day-old baby with a rare heart defect at the center of a complex surrogacy dispute in Texas has been handed over to the parents’ custody and is receiving care, lawyers for the parents said on Friday.

The baby has hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a defect that requires surgeries to correct. The baby was born on Wednesday to surrogate mother McKenna West of Alaska after she reportedly refused requests to get an abortion from the biological parents, Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed of California – requests they deny making.

Continue reading...
title: Baby with heart defect at center of US surrogacy dispute handed to parents

author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
description:
With questions over Farage’s finances and a new face in No 10, could Barnsley council be a bellwether for changing Labour fortunes?

Labour marked its worst performance in more than 50 years when voters went to the polls in Barnsley in May, but 100 days on from those seismic local elections, the political landscape has shifted drastically.

Could the South Yorkshire town, where Reform UK reaped the benefits of dissatisfaction with Labour, prove to be a test case for whether the governing party has turned the tide?

Continue reading...
title: ‘Let’s see what he can do’: will Burnham bring Barnsley voters back to Labour?

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Utility company’s plant, which has only run five times, now has an estimated total cost of £500m

Thames Water is preparing the UK’s only desalination plant to restart operations later this year – but it will only be ready in the winter, long after the current drought is likely to have passed.

The utility company said that it was hoping to start operating its plant in Beckton, east London, “by the end of the year”, in order to help build up reservoir supplies over the winter for next summer.

Continue reading...
title: Thames Water plans to restart desalination plant – after drought has ended

author: Ashifa Kassam in Madrid
description:
Marine conservationist says deliberate attack would be ‘act of extreme cruelty’ against endangered population

Spanish officials have launched an investigation after the matriarch of an orca pod known for jostling and ramming boats off the Iberian Peninsula was spotted with wounds suggesting she had been shot by a pellet gun.

On Friday, Spain’s environment ministry said Toñi, the oldest living member of the pod, had been seen swimming in the Strait of Gibraltar with markings on her dorsal fin that were “consistent with shots from a pellet gun”.

Continue reading...
title: Iberian orca known for ramming boats seen with suspected gunshot wounds

author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
description:
UK team seeking to put suitcase-sized satellite in orbit around moon in search for 21cm line radio frequency signal

Little is known about what was happening shortly after the big bang, but now researchers are hoping to shed fresh light on the matter by harnessing the dark side of the moon.

Scientists are hoping to put a suitcase-sized satellite into orbit around the moon, using the data it collects as it passes the far side to search for a radio frequency signal emitted by neutral hydrogen atoms in the early universe.

Continue reading...
title: Scientists hope to shed light on young universe by using dark side of the moon

author: Ima Caldwell
description:
The administrative work required to run an effective investment scam has been drastically cut by using merging technology

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Within days of clicking on an online ad for a cryptocurrency trading app, a 29-year-old Queensland man watched his dashboard soar with profits.

Making investment gains was as simple as downloading the slick-looking app and browser extension linked to his crypto wallet. So he invested more.

Continue reading...
title: A Queensland man enjoyed soaring profits from a crypto trading app. Then his money started disappearing

author: Morwenna Ferrier
description:
Mod fashion, nod to 80s excess or symbol of tradition? Andy Burnham’s wardrobe choice transcends class divisions

The sartorial evolution of Andy Burnham reached another milestone this week when the prime minister appeared at a photocall in Derbyshire wearing a pair of braces under his suit.

Navy, slimline and button-on rather than clipped, they were barely visible while he posed for a photo in Ilkeston. It was only when he unbuttoned his suit jacket to embrace members of the public that they were on view.

Continue reading...
title: Belt and braces PM: what wearing suit braces says about Burnham

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Earlier this week prosecutors and Luigi Mangione’s lawyers filed a joint letter requesting the hearing at 11am on Friday in Manhattan federal court

This morning, the Guardian chatted with Seth Zuckerman, founder of Zuckerman Legal Group and a former New York prosecutor, to run through the process we might expect this morning.

If Mangione were to plead guilty, the proceeding will start with both sides telling Judge Margaret Garnett that a plea is going to take place.

Continue reading...
title: Luigi Mangione to appear in court amid reports of plea deal over healthcare CEO’s killing – live

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
Move will be one of first large-scale foreign investments in country since US ousted leader Nicolás Maduro in January

BP has answered Donald Trump’s call for oil companies to help rebuild Venezuela’s fossil fuel industry with new plans to develop a large offshore gasfield.

BP will partner with two oil firms with close links to the Trump administration to develop the second phase of the Loran gasfield, in one of the first large-scale foreign investments in Venezuela since the US ousted its leader Nicolás Maduro in January.

Continue reading...
title: BP to develop offshore gasfield in Venezuela with firms linked to Trump administration

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Possible cut from 80% down to as little as 50% could add millions of tonnes of CO2 to emissions and comes amid UK heatwaves

Andy Burnham’s government has said it will look at cutting electric vehicle sales targets, in proposals that could add millions of tonnes a year to the UK’s future carbon dioxide emissions.

The government launched a consultation on Friday on cutting the target for new EVs to as little as 50% of all new cars in 2030, down from 80% under existing rules. The consultation will include several options, including leaving the headline target unchanged, or cutting it to 70%, 60% or 50%.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham moves to cut new EV sales targets

author: Pjotr Sauer
description:
Russia is losing 30,000 casualties a month, and the country’s regions are under pressure to feed the ‘meat-grinder’. Experts say it may not be enough

In kitchens and Telegram chats across Russia, the same question is being asked with growing frequency: will Vladimir Putin order another mobilisation?

Nearly five years into the war, Russia is scrambling to find enough soldiers to replenish its ranks, as voluntary recruitment slows and its forces suffer heavy losses on the battlefield in Ukraine.

Continue reading...
title: Putin’s recruiters scramble to avoid second mass mobilisation as Ukraine losses mount

author: Reuters
description:
Interior department calls incident ‘utter disgrace’ after area filled with bubbles and paint reading ‘Clean hands Dirty $’

A memorial in Washington DC for the second world war was vandalized with bubbly ⁠soap and graffiti on Thursday, prompting vows from the US government to find the perpetrator.

The fountain bubbled over with suds ⁠and someone painted “Clean hands Dirty $” ⁠on one ​surface, splattering the area with red and green paint. Uniformed police and national guard troops converged on the scene, which was ⁠cordoned off with yellow crime scene tape, keeping visitors away.

Continue reading...
title: Memorial for second world war vandalized with bubbles and graffiti in Washington

author: Simon Hattenstone
description:
Lawyer says restriction comes at ‘significant moment’ in appeal process for White House Farm murder conviction

The legal team of Jeremy Bamber, who has served 41 years in prison for murdering five members of his family, has challenged Wakefield prison’s decision to ban him from talking about his case to the media and long-term supporters.

His lawyers have issued a claim for judicial review against the secretary of state for justice and the governor of the category A high-security prison, arguing that it is violating his right to free speech and obstructing his access to justice.

Continue reading...
title: Jeremy Bamber’s legal team challenge ban on his talking to the media

author: Press Association
description:
Steven Sansom and Adam Watson accused of trying to kill Urfan Sharif, who murdered his daughter, in Belmarsh prison

Two men have been charged with attempted murder after the father of the murdered schoolgirl Sara Sharif was attacked in prison.

Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, are accused of trying to kill Urfan Sharif at HMP Belmarsh on New Year’s Day last year.

Continue reading...
title: Two men charged with attempted murder of Sara Sharif’s father

author: Emma Brockes
description:
Plus, heartbreakingly brilliant Cats: the Jellicle Ball, summer reads and Taylor Swift’s low-key wedding

I’ve been in New York for two weeks, where the unthinkable has happened: even for a city accustomed to extremes, it is so hot, so humid, so reminiscent of Mobile, Alabama, or Mumbai, that all over the city, New Yorkers have been forced to break persona to talk about the weather. “Was it always like this?” (No.) “Can you believe this?” (No.) “Are you having a stroke?” (Possibly.)

Continue reading...
title: Digested week: Humid New York or London’s oven-blast heat? Tough one to call

author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem and Rowena Mason
description:
Israeli PM criticised by political rival for attacking an international ally and overseeing ‘horrific diplomatic failure’

The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, called the UK “the Islamic republic of Britain” in a podcast interview, where he also described the country as the “first Islamic republic to get a nuclear weapon”.

His comments, made during an interview for Israel’s army radio, played into a common far-right Islamophobic trope about Britain’s small Muslim population.

Continue reading...
title: Benjamin Netanyahu describes UK as ‘first Islamic republic to get a nuclear weapon’

author: Mabel Banfield-Nwachi
description:
President visiting police academy in Long Island as he looks to boost Republicans in battleground races ahead of November midterms

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

This week’s Politics Weekly America looks at Trump’s plane ruse. The President departed on a secret military flight from Turkey to Britain last month, prompted by an Iranian assassination threat. Almost everyone believed he was on Air Force One, turns out he wasn’t.

You can hear all about the elaborate scheme to protect the President here.
title: Donald Trump to give speech on crime and safety during New York visit – US politics live

author: Martin Belam
description:
Undercover agents infiltrated meetings, private chats and local events. Plus Wile E Coyote returns to the big screen

Good morning. The extent to which federal law enforcement targeted political opponents and peaceful organizers has been laid bare in newly disclosed court documents.

Internal investigative files reveal that the Department of Homeland Security launched a sweeping surveillance operation against anti-ICE protesters, major labor unions and left-leaning advocacy groups – sending undercover agents to infiltrate community meetings and issuing administrative subpoenas to seize financial records. The documents show that DHS investigators obtained financial records of unions and non-profits, as part of an inquiry into “domestic terrorist financing”.

What did undercover government agents do? They infiltrated community meetings, joined private
title: First Thing: Court files show how federal agents spied on anti-ICE protesters | Martin Belam

author: Adria R Walker
description:
Ben Crump and Rev Al Sharpton, also present at National Association of Black Journalists, demanded ‘truth’ and ‘transparency’ in Wells’ case

On Thursday morning, the parents of Nolan Wells, Christine Wells-Wonsley and Elmore Wonsley, along with Ben Crump, the civil rights attorney, and Rev Al Sharpton, the famed civil rights activist, spoke at the National Association of Black Journalists (NABJ) convention in Atlanta. Wells was an 18-year-old college student who was found dead on 6 July after a boating trip with friends, and his death captured national attention.

Wells went missing on 4 July and a photo of the teen, who was Black, and his three friends on the trip, who were white, went viral. Social media users have speculated that Wells’s disappearance, death and the perceived lack of urgency in the county’s investigation into what happened to the teen are be
title: Nolan Wells’ parents recount ordeal of son’s death at Atlanta convention

author: Victoria Bekiempis in New York
description:
Mangione also faces separate state trial over killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in Manhattan, due to start on 8 September

A hurriedly scheduled hearing for Luigi Mangione’s federal case in the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson is set for later on Friday morning, fueling speculation that he might plead guilty in these proceedings.

Mangione faces two stalking counts in his federal case, as well as murder and weapons charges in a separate New York state case. He has pleaded not guilty in both cases. Both the federal and state cases could lead to a life prison sentence.

Continue reading...
title: Luigi Mangione hearing fuels speculation of a guilty plea in federal case

author: Megan Davies for MetDesk
description:
England received only 10% of its average July rainfall and some areas may just get the odd shower for rest of August

England has experienced its driest July since records began in 1836, receiving only 6.5mm of rainfall – 10% of the country’s long-term meteorological average for the month. Wales also experienced its driest-ever July, while Northern Ireland recorded it was its eighth driest. Scotland was the only country in the UK not to set new records but still received only 69% of its average rainfall for July compared with the long-term average. Southern England has faced the worst of the dry conditions with some areas, including the Sussex coast, receiving less than 0.2mm of rain in July. This has resulted in widespread low moisture content within the soil, enabling temperatures to reach the high 30s celsius.

Looking ahead, despite notable spells of rain in the north, parts of southern England may receive only the odd shower for the rest of August. Throughout summer,
title: Little rain on the horizon as England and Wales experience driest July on record

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
The Reform UK leader forced a vote that failed to make financial questions disappear, only the man himself

• Clacton byelection – UK politics live

Dawn had long broken in the Essex town of Clacton-on-Sea when the results for the byelection came in. After a gruelling count, an atmosphere of deep exhaustion had settled over the room. Even the man with a dustbin on his head looked weary.

As it was declared that Nigel Farage had, as expected, won, there was no cheering in the room, which had been boycotted by the Reform UK leader and his supporters; instead there was only an overwhelming sense of futility.
title: Futile Clacton byelection has done Farage no favours

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Reform UK leader’s return to Clacton restarts inquiry into £5m gift from cyrpto-billionaire and support from fraudster

The suspended parliamentary standards investigation into Nigel Farage over accusations he failed to declare gifts and donations has resumed after the Reform UK leader’s re-election as the MP for Clacton.

The twofold investigation by Daniel Greenberg, the parliamentary commissioner for standards, was paused after Farage resigned from his seat and called a byelection in protest at what he said was unfair scrutiny of his finances.

Continue reading...
title: Standards watchdog resumes investigation into Nigel Farage over financial gifts

author: Sarah Basford Canales and Krishani Dhanji
description:
Greens say Labor’s reform set to ‘rip life-changing supports away from disabled people instead of raising additional revenue through taxing gas exports’

Cross-benchers have slammed the Albanese government’s proposed overhaul of the NDIS as going “too far, too fast” as the changes to curb the growth of the $52bn program appear set to pass the parliament as early as next week.

The Greens and independent ACT senator, David Pocock, delivered scathing assessments of the bill they warn will enable blunt and indiscriminate cuts to individual budgets supporting more than 770,000 Australians with disabilities in a final Senate inquiry report released on Friday afternoon.

Continue reading...
title: Pocock and crossbenchers call Labor’s NDIS overhaul ‘too far, too fast’ in scathing Senate inquiry report

author: Cait Kelly
description:
ABS data shows an almost 9% slump in new lending to investors after three interest rate hikes this year

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

In what one economist is describing as a “tiny step” toward a fairer housing market after decades of bad policy, property investors are shying away fr
title: Lending to property investors falls sharply in ‘tiny’ step towards fairer housing market in Australia, expert says

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Independent Education Union ‘deeply concerned … public funding for Catholic schools may have been wrongfully spent on Liberal party matters’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The union for independent school teachers in New South Wales has demanded greater scrutiny of Catholic schools as the chief executive of their governing body told a corruption inquiry payments to a lobbying firm were not a “sham arrangement” to fund Liberal party factional work.

Dallas McInerney insisted to the NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Friday that Catholic Schools NSW funding wasn’t misused.
title: Teachers demand more scrutiny of Catholic school funding amid allegations of ‘sham arrangement’ with NSW Liberal group

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Preliminary findings show fan blade broke off shortly after takeoff on 10 July flight from Greece to Germany

Broken engine parts were responsible for shattering a window on a Ryanair plane, causing a passenger to be partly sucked out mid-flight in July, US investigators have said.

A preliminary report by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) found an engine fan blade broke off shortly after takeoff on the 10 July flight from Greece to Germany.

Continue reading...
title: Engine parts shattered Ryanair window that passenger was partly sucked out of, report says

author: Sammy Gecsoyler
description:
Reform UK leader does not appear for the result, despite beating nearest challenger, Count Binface, in byelection he caused amid deepening scandal over £5m gift

  • Clacton byelection – UK politics live

Nigel Farage has seen off Count Binface to win the Clacton byelection in a contest boycotted by every other major political party.

The Reform UK leader in July triggered the byelection in an attempt to shake off a deepening scandal over a £5m gift he received from the cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne.
title: Nigel Farage wins Clacton byelection in contest boycotted by every other major party

author: Helena Horton and Deborah Solomon
description:
From chefs to paramedics, workers tell the Guardian how they are coping and unions outline the changes needed in the workplace

In the sweltering kitchen of the Plimsoll pub in north London, the head chef, Joshua Swinney, has a frozen tea towel wrapped around his neck to combat the heat.

As temperatures exceeded 35C (95F) in the capital, workers who were not lucky enough to be in air-conditioned offices sweltered in the heat.

Continue reading...
title: Builders, bakers and cheeseburger-makers: the UK workers struggling in extreme heat

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Interim report calls for carve-up deal that has only benefited Western Australia to be ‘reshaped’ as it has achieved almost none of its objectives

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Productivity Commission (PC) has criticised the controversial GST deal with Western Australia as a costly mistake that sh
title: Morrison-era GST deal with WA a multi-billion dollar mistake that should be reversed, Productivity Commission finds

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Airservices boss says planes remained 1km apart so runway incursion ‘didn’t meet mandatory reporting requirements’ but safety bureau is ‘concerned’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The organisation that manages Australian skies has defended its decision not to immediately report a fresh safety incident at Sydney airport when a Virgin plane aborted its take-off.

The chief executive of the commonwealth-owned Airservices A
title: Sydney airport incident involving Virgin and Qantas flights didn’t have to be reported, Airservices Australia says

author: Adam Fulton and Tom Ambrose
description:
The Reform UK leader will not be present at vote count in byelection he has tried to frame as the ‘people versus the establishment’

  • Nigel Farage set for decisive but arguably empty victory in Clacton

Nigel Farage has said he will not attend the Clacton byelection count after advice from Essex police about a plot to embarrass him on stage during the announcement of the result.

The Reform UK leader pre-empted the official announcement of the result of the byelection by telling supporters he had secured more votes than when he won the seat at the 2024 general election.

Continue reading...
title: Nigel Farage says he won’t attend count in Clacton byelection against Count Binface - UK politics live

author: Amanda Meade and Kat Wong
description:
Former 2UE and 2GB radio broadcaster is facing 22 indecent assault and sexual touching charges. Jones, 85, has pleaded not guilty

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A driver for Alan Jones aspired to be a producer but was required to make the 2GB host’s breakfast of soft-boiled eggs with bread soldiers, clean his bathroom at the radio station and iron underpants, a Sydney court has heard.

Complainant C told Jones’s indece
title: Alleged victim of Alan Jones made broadcaster soft-boiled eggs with soldiers and ironed his underpants, court told

author: Isabella Lee
description:
Shizuoka Crown melons are part of an important cultural gifting practice in Japan, where they are hand-patted by growers to achieve an even shape and texture

The melons at the centre of a national imbroglio involving the Australian prime minister have the sweetness of a watermelon, the snap of a honeydew and the perfume of a peach, according to fruit sellers.

Anthony Albanese maintains he has nothing to apologise for, after a joke he made regarding a gift he received from Japan’s prime minister.

Continue reading...
title: Australia has been galvanised by ‘melon-gate’. So what is the luxury fruit at the centre of the PM’s controversy?
